properties.title: Post Incident Review (PIR) – Entra ID Application – Permissions management issues
properties.description:
What happened?

You were identified among a subset of Entra ID application customers trying to update application configurations that target consumer accounts, who may have experienced problems saving configuration changes. Updates may have failed through the user interface as well as via APIs, between 19:00 UTC on 8 September 2024 and 04:40 UTC on 12 September 2024. Authentications were not impacted. While this issue impacted less than 15% of Microsoft Entra Permissions Management operations during this time period, unfortunately it impacted one or more of your Azure subscriptions. That’s why we’re providing you with this Post Incident Review (PIR) – to summarize what went wrong, how we responded, and the steps Microsoft is taking to learn from this and improve.


What went wrong and why?

Updates to app configurations in Entra ID that targeted consumer apps failed to save to the backend. These updates are encrypted prior to being saved; however this process began failing because the encryption key that was being used had been revoked. Because there was no other available key to perform the encryption, these updates failed to save properly. This key revocation was a planned routine activity and was not due to any security incident.

How did we respond?

This incident was initially reported to us by an impacted customer, as our current monitoring did not include this scenario. The mitigation involved providing a new valid encryption key for Entra ID to utilize for saving app configurations for consumer apps. A new key was rolled out globally in a gradual fashion, and 99.9% of customers recovered within 6 hours. Full recovery was achieved about 24 hours later.

properties.title: Post Incident Review (PIR) – Microsoft Entra ID Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) – Sign-in logs
properties.description:
What happened?

You were impacted by a platform issue that caused some of our customers to experience issues with sign-in logs for Microsoft Entra ID Multi-factor authentication (MFA), between 16:00 UTC on 19 June 2024 and 19:45 UTC on 28 July 2024. During this period, sign-in logs might not have included the error results of MFA attempts. For example, if an MFA challenge resulted in a notification in the Microsoft Authenticator App, and the user selected “No, it’s not me”, the exact error result for this was not logged. This issue was observed in the Azure Portal, the Microsoft Graph API, and in Log Analytics. Sign-in logs continued to include successful sign-in attempts and all errors in other scenarios. This also included the error code for the MFA challenge itself, which correctly showed users as interrupted. We’re providing you with this Post Incident Review (PIR) to summarize what went wrong, how we responded, and the steps Microsoft is taking to learn from this and improve.


What went wrong and why?

A code change was introduced on 19 June to improve the display of application information in MFA flows in Entra ID sign-in logs. This change included a bug, where the tenant ID stopped being logged in the completion stage of the MFA flow by the Entra ID authentication service. The lack of tenant ID in internal logs meant that the Entra ID log processor, responsible for publishing sign-in logs to customers, could not associate log entries with individual tenants. The led to logs being dropped and missing in sign-in logs.


How did we respond?

After the code bug was introduced, unfortunately it was not detected by test cases, or by automatic deployment qualification gates. The issue was also not detected by the Entra ID log processor service, only being reported to Microsoft on 17 July 2024, 20 days after it was introduced. After the relevant engineering team was engaged, the issue was diagnosed, and we began working on a hotfix. The hotfix deployment started 20 July but, due to increased caution around changes during that time, the change went through an extended Safe Deployment Practices (SDP) period. The deployment completed at 20:45 UTC on 28 July, although all customer impact was fully mitigated by 19:45 UTC on 28 July - individual tenants may have seen recovery even earlier.


How are we making incidents like this less likely or less impactful?

  • We have developed and deployed a hotfix fixing this specific issue with the code change described above. (Completed)
  • We have increased test coverage for these specific scenarios, asserting that the tenant ID is always logged in MFA flows. (Completed)
  • We are reviewing our deployment gates and adding new conditions for missing key telemetry data points. (Estimated completion: September 2024)
  • We are evaluating gaps in detection by the sign-in log processor, to develop monitors for dropped log entries. (Estimated completion: September 2024)

  • Generally, consider evaluating the reliability of your applications using guidance from the Azure Well-Architected Framework and its interactive Well-Architected Review: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/framework/resiliency

properties.summary: Post Incident Review (PIR) – Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management – Performance issue with Role Actions
properties.description:
Post Incident Review (PIR) – Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management – Performance issue with Role Actions


What happened?

You were impacted by a platform issue that caused some of our Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) customers to experience issues performing various actions like role activations, approvals, adding assignments, and similar. These issues happened between 14:38 UTC and 17:48 UTC on 24 July 2024, during which period scheduled role assignments' deactivations may also have been delayed. While this issue impacted less than 4% of Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management customers, unfortunately, it impacted one or more of your Azure subscriptions. That’s why we’re providing you with this Post Incident Review (PIR) – to summarize what went wrong, how we responded, and the steps Microsoft is taking to learn from this and improve.

 

What went wrong and why?

PIM supports applications that only make calls to fetch PIM entities, such as active and eligible role assignments. However, a multi-tenant registered application began making calls across multiple tenants simultaneously in large volumes, causing a significant load on our backend database. This spike in activity led our backend to run at full capacity, resulting in some users experiencing timeout errors from the APIs. During this spike, we identified two issues that contributed to the incident. First, our throttling policy limit did not effectively reduce the load. Second, under extreme load our backend queries were not performing optimally to return results from the backend.

 

How did we respond?

Our monitoring system detected the issue within a minute and alerted our on-call engineers. We quickly implemented mitigation steps to resolve the problem and restore service health - these steps included enhancing the throttling policy to reduce the call load on our service backend, and updating our backend to use performant queries for faster results. Although these measures helped to alleviate the load on our service and backend, it took longer than expected for the changes to take effect and bring the service back to a healthy state. We are committed to ensuring that such scenarios do not recur in the future.

 

How are we making incidents like this less likely or less impactful?

  • We have enhanced our throttling policy to reduce the call load on our service and backend. (Completed)
  • We are now enforcing performant queries on our backend. (Completed)
  • We are working towards identifying additional scenarios that could impact the load on our service, so that we can enhance the throttling policy to address them. (Estimated completion: August 2024)
  • In the longer term, we are working to reduce load on active regions by using non-active regions to serve application read-only calls. (Estimated completion: September 2024)

 

How can customers make incidents like this less impactful?

  • There was nothing that customers could have done to reduce impact from this incident impacting role activations, assignments, and similar operations.
  • More generally, consider evaluating the reliability of your mission-critical applications using guidance from the Azure Well-Architected Framework and its interactive Well-Architected Review: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/framework/resiliency

If you have questions, please contact us.

properties.title: Important notice: Upcoming TLS changes for Azure Event Grid
properties.summary: You're receiving this notice because you're using Azure Event Grid.
properties.description:
You're receiving this notice because you're using Azure Event Grid.

To enhance security and provide best-in-class encryption for your data, we'll require Azure Event Grid to be secured using Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 or later beginning 31 October 2024, when support for TLS 1.0 and 1.1 will end. In addition to continuing support for TLS 1.2, we will enable TLS 1.3 for Azure Event Grid on 31 October 2024.

If you're using TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1 for Azure Event Grid topics or domains, you'll need to switch to TLS 1.2 or later by 31 October 2024. If you're using Azure Event Grid namespaces, no action is required.

Required action

If you're not using the minimum required version, switch to TLS 1.2 or later by 31 October 2024. If you're using Azure Event Grid system topics, follow the instructions in our API documentation or SDK documentation.

Once you enforce the minimum TLS version, make sure that events continue flowing in your test and production environments.

Help and support

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, open the Azure portal and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.

properties.summary: You’re receiving this email because one or more of your consumption SKU logic apps could be affected by an upcoming change.
properties.description:

To improve traffic flow, we’re adding new IP addresses for Azure Logic Apps. If you have firewall configurations that have allow list Logic Apps IP addresses, you’ll need to update them to keep your logic apps running as expected.

Please note this only affects consumption SKU logic apps and not standard SKU logic apps.

If you don’t have this type of firewall configuration, you won’t be affected by this change and don’t need to take any action.

Required action

Update your firewall configurations to include the IP addresses below by 12 November 2024.

If you have questions, please contact us.

properties.title: Action required: Migrate to Azure Monitor Agent by 31 August 2024
properties.summary: You’re receiving this message because you’re still using the Log Analytics Agent which’ll no longer be supported on 31 August 2024.
properties.description:
You’re receiving this message because you’re still using the Log Analytics Agent which’ll no longer be supported on 31 August 2024. 

On 31 August 2024, the Log Analytics Agent will be retired. To ensure continued usage of Azure Virtual Desktop Insights, you need to migrate to the Azure Monitor Agent by this date. Users who continue to use the deprecated Log Analytics Agent will no longer be able to view session host data, such as performance and event details, in Azure Virtual Desktop Insights.

Contact your Azure Global Administrator for Azure Virtual Desktop to develop a plan for deploying these updates to your infrastructure. Update your internal documentation as needed and inform your helpdesk about this change, if applicable.

Required action

To avoid any service disruptions, migrate to the Azure Monitor Agent by 31 August 2024. Review our updated configuration process in the Azure Virtual Desktop Insights documentation.

Help and support

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and need technical help, please create a support request.

properties.title: Action recommended: Regenerate your Azure Event Grid shared access signature key
properties.summary: You're receiving this notice because you're using Azure Event Grid.
properties.description:
You're receiving this notice because you're using Azure Event Grid.

For increased security, Azure Event Grid will update the length of shared access signature (SAS) keys from 44 to 84 characters for all regions from 5 August 2024 to 15 August 2024. After that, all new or regenerated SAS keys will have a length of 84 characters.

Recommended action

While this change will not impact any application and service currently publishing events to Event Grid, we recommend regenerating your key on or after 15 August 2024 to enhance your security. After regenerating the key, update any event publishing application or services that were using the old key.

Help and support

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, open the Azure portal and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.

Retirements.Header: Your service might have been impacted by an Azure service issue
Retirements.Description:
You’re receiving this message because you’re still using the Log Analytics Agent which’ll no longer be supported on 31 August 2024. 

On 31 August 2024, the Log Analytics Agent will be retired. To ensure continued usage of Azure Virtual Desktop Insights, you need to migrate to the Azure Monitor Agent by this date. Users who continue to use the deprecated Log Analytics Agent will no longer be able to view session host data, such as performance and event details, in Azure Virtual Desktop Insights.

Contact your Azure Global Administrator for Azure Virtual Desktop to develop a plan for deploying these updates to your infrastructure. Update your internal documentation as needed and inform your helpdesk about this change, if applicable.

Required action

To avoid any service disruptions, migrate to the Azure Monitor Agent by 31 August 2024. Review our updated configuration process in the Azure Virtual Desktop Insights documentation.

Help and support

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and need technical help, please create a support request.
